verbatim_evidence_quote: Avermectins are produced by Streptomyces avermitilis MA-4680 (NRRL 8165), isolated by Omura et al. from a soil sample collected near a golf course at Kawana, Shizuoka Prefecture, Japan.
Bti was first isolated from a water pond in the Negev desert (Goldberg & Margalit, 1977) and commercialized for dipteran vector control.
Discovery of highly active Bacillus thuringiensis subspecies kurstaki strain HD-1 by Dulmage (1970) from diseased pink bollworm larvae in Brownsville, Texas.

envo_material_id: diseased Mediterranean flour moth larva (Ephestia kuehniella)
verbatim_evidence_quote: Officially described by Berliner in 1915, isolated from Mediterranean flour moth in the province of Thuringia in 1911; first commercialized as Sporeine in France in 1938.
Bacillus thuringiensis serovar aizawai (H7) was isolated in Japan from silkworm rearing litter/larvae and commercialized against lepidopteran pests.
A new antibiotic, SF-1293 (bialaphos), was isolated from the culture filtrate of Streptomyces hygroscopicus SF-1293, which was isolated from a soil sample collected in Japan.
Blasticidin S, a new antibiotic produced by Streptomyces griseochromogenes, was isolated from a soil sample in Japan and found to inhibit Piricularia oryzae.
Streptomyces kasugaensis was isolated from a soil sample collected at the Kasuga shrine in Nara Prefecture, Japan.
Strain B-41-146, classified as Streptomyces hygroscopicus subsp. aureolacrimosus, was isolated from a soil sample collected in Hokkaido, Japan.
Mildiomycin is produced by Streptoverticillium rimofaciens B-98891, which was isolated from a soil sample collected at Nikko, Tochigi Prefecture, Japan.
Terramycin (oxytetracycline) is produced by Streptomyces rimosus, isolated from a soil sample collected near Terre Haute, Indiana (dual clinical and agricultural bactericide).
Polyoxins are produced by Streptomyces cacaoi var. asoensis, isolated from a soil sample collected at Mt. Aso, Kumamoto Prefecture, Japan.

envo_material_id: soil from abandoned sugar-cane rum still
verbatim_evidence_quote: Saccharopolyspora spinosa was isolated from a soil sample collected in 1982 from an abandoned rum still on a Caribbean island (Virgin Islands).
Streptomyces hygroscopicus var. limoneus No. T-7545 was isolated from a soil sample collected in Akashi, Hyogo Prefecture, Japan.
Azotobacter vinelandii produces an extracellular polyuronide closely resembling algal alginic acid.
Bacterium xylinum forms a tough, gelatinous membrane on the surface of vinegar fermentations which gives all the chemical reactions of pure cellulose.
Alcaligenes faecalis var. myxogenes 10C3, isolated from soil in Osaka, produces a neutral gel-forming beta-1,3-glucan named curdlan.
Dextrans produced by Leuconostoc mesenteroides NRRL B-512F were characterized for clinical plasma-volume expander production.
An extracellular homo-poly-amino acid of L-lysine was found in the culture filtrate of Streptomyces albulus No. 346, isolated from soil.

envo_material_id: Elodea aquatic plant tissue in freshwater pond
verbatim_evidence_quote: Pseudomonas elodea ATCC 31461, isolated from an Elodea water plant, produces an extracellular linear anionic heteropolysaccharide (gellan).
Mucoid strains of hemolytic streptococci synthesize a capsular polysaccharide identical to mammalian hyaluronic acid.
Bacterial levan, a beta-2,6-linked fructan, is synthesized extracellularly from sucrose by Zymomonas mobilis and Bacillus subtilis.
Bacillus megaterium accumulates intracellular granules of poly-beta-hydroxybutyric acid as a carbon and energy reserve.
Alcaligenes eutrophus H16, isolated from sludge/water in Gottingen, was developed by ICI for industrial production of P(3HB-co-3HV) copolymer.
Bacillus subtilis (natto) produces extracellular poly-gamma-glutamic acid as the main viscous component of fermented soybeans.
Xanthomonas campestris NRRL B-1459 produces an extracellular heteropolysaccharide (xanthan) in commercial aerobic fermentation.
Strain MIS38, isolated from a soil sample in Japan, produces a potent cyclic lipoundecapeptide biosurfactant designated arthrofactin.
Acinetobacter calcoaceticus RAG-1, isolated from seawater at a Tel Aviv beach, produces an extracellular polyanionic bioemulsifier (emulsan).
Fengycin, an antifungal lipopeptide complex, is produced by Bacillus subtilis F-29-3 isolated from soil of a potato farm in Taipei, Taiwan.
Iturin A is an antifungal cyclic lipopeptide produced by a Bacillus subtilis strain originally isolated from soil in the Ituri region of the Congo.
Bacillus licheniformis JF-2, isolated from oil-field injection water in Oklahoma, anaerobically produces a potent lipopeptide biosurfactant (lichenysin).
A crystalline glycolipid composed of L-rhamnose and beta-hydroxydecanoic acid was isolated from cultures of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
Serratia marcescens produces an extracellular cyclodepsipeptide wetting agent designated serrawettin W1.
Surfactin, a crystalline peptidelipid surfactant with extremely high surface activity, was isolated from culture broth of Bacillus subtilis IAM 1213.
Viscosin, an acidic crystalline peptide antibiotic and surface-active agent, was isolated from Pseudomonas viscosa isolated from soil in Tokyo.
Bacitracin is produced by a gram-positive sporulating bacillus (Tracy I) isolated from tissue debrided from a compound fracture of the tibia in patient Margaret Tracy.
Bleomycin was discovered in culture filtrates of Streptomyces verticillus, isolated from a soil sample collected at Oga Peninsula, Akita Prefecture, Japan.
Capreomycin is a peptide antibiotic complex produced by Streptomyces capreolus NRRL 2773, isolated from a soil sample.
Chloromycetin is produced by an actinomycete (Streptomyces venezuelae) isolated by Paul R. Burkholder from a soil sample collected in a mulched field near Caracas, Venezuela.
Clavulanic acid, a potent beta-lactamase inhibitor, is produced by Streptomyces clavuligerus ATCC 27064 (NRRL 3585).
Cycloserine (D-4-amino-3-isoxazolidone) was independently isolated from soil actinomycetes Streptomyces orchidaceus and Streptomyces garyphalus.
Actinomycin was isolated from cultures of Actinomyces antibioticus isolated from soil at the New Jersey Agricultural Experiment Station.
Ferrioxamine B was isolated from Streptomyces pilosus ETH 21748, obtained from a soil sample collected at Torre del Lago, Italy.
Dihydrostreptomycin was prepared by catalytic hydrogenation of streptomycin from Streptomyces griseus and later found directly in Streptomyces humidus.
Ilotycin (erythromycin) is produced by a strain of Streptomyces erythreus isolated from a soil sample collected in the Philippine Archipelago (Iloilo) by Abelardo Aguilar.
Tiacumicins are produced by Dactylosporangium aurantiacum subsp. hamdenensis AB 718C-41, isolated from a soil sample collected in Hamden, Connecticut.
Phosphonomycin (fosfomycin) is produced by Streptomyces fradiae ATCC 21096, isolated from a soil sample collected in Spain.
Gentamicin is a broad-spectrum antibiotic complex produced by Micromonospora purpurea, isolated from a soil sample collected in Syracuse, New York.
Kanamycin was isolated from a new species Streptomyces kanamyceticus obtained from a soil sample collected in Nagano Prefecture, Japan.
Lincomycin is produced by Streptomyces lincolnensis var. lincolnensis NRRL 2936, isolated from soil collected near Lincoln, Nebraska.
1-Deoxygalactonojirimycin (migalastat) was isolated as a natural alpha-galactosidase inhibitor from Streptomyces lydicus PA-5726 (commercial API synthesized).
Mitomycin C was isolated from Streptomyces caespitosus obtained from a soil sample collected in Tokyo, Japan.
Pseudomonic acid (mupirocin) is an antibiotic produced by Pseudomonas fluorescens NCIMB 10586.
Pimaricin (natamycin) is produced by Streptomyces natalensis, isolated from a soil sample collected near Pietermaritzburg in Natal, South Africa.
Neomycin is produced by a soil actinomycete closely related to Streptomyces fradiae isolated at the New Jersey Agricultural Experiment Station.
Streptonivicin (novobiocin) is produced by Streptomyces niveus n. sp., isolated from a soil sample collected in Queens Village, New York.
2'-Deoxycoformycin (pentostatin) was isolated from fermentation broths of Streptomyces antibioticus NRRL 3238.
Polymyxin is produced by Bacillus polymyxa isolated from soil samples in Pearl River, New York.
Rifomycin is produced by Streptomyces mediterranei sp. nov., isolated from a soil sample collected in a pine forest near St. Raphael, France.
FR901228 (romidepsin), a novel bicyclic depsipeptide antitumor antibiotic, is produced by Chromobacterium violaceum No. 968 isolated from a soil sample collected in Yamagata Prefecture, Japan.
Rapamycin is an antifungal antibiotic produced by Streptomyces hygroscopicus NRRL 5491, isolated from an Easter Island (Rapa Nui) soil sample.
Actinospectacin (spectinomycin) is produced by Streptomyces spectabilis NRRL 2494, isolated from a soil sample.
Streptomycin was isolated from Actinomyces griseus obtained from a heavily manured field soil at the New Jersey Agricultural Experiment Station.
FK-506 (tacrolimus) is produced by Streptomyces tsukubaensis No. 9993, isolated from a soil sample collected at Tsukuba, Ibaraki Prefecture, Japan.
3,5-Dihydroxy-4-isopropylstilbene (tapinarof) is produced by Xenorhabdus luminescens isolated from insect-parasitic nematodes in Australia.
Nebramycin (factor 6 = tobramycin) is produced by Streptomyces tenebrarius, isolated from a soil sample collected in Mexico.
Ecteinascidin 743 (trabectedin) is produced by the uncultured bacterial symbiont Candidatus Endoecteinascidia frumentensis associated with the Caribbean tunicate Ecteinascidia turbinata.
Agrobacterium aurantiacum N-81106 (Paracoccus sp.), isolated from coastal seawater in Japan, synthesizes (3S,3'S)-astaxanthin.
Canthaxanthin is the major carotenoid pigment synthesized by photosynthetic Bradyrhizobium strains and Gordonia jacobaea MV-1.
Indigoidine, a blue diaza-diphenoquinone pigment, is produced extracellularly by Pseudomonas indigofera (Vogesella indigofera).
C-Phycocyanin is a brilliant blue phycobiliprotein pigment commercially extracted from the cyanobacterium Arthrospira platensis.
Prodigiosin, the characteristic red tripyrrole pigment of Serratia marcescens (Bacillus prodigiosus), was isolated and crystallized from bacterial cultures.
Pyocyanin, the blue phenazine pigment of Bacillus pyocyaneus (Pseudomonas aeruginosa), was isolated from clinical wound dressings.
Commercial industrial fermentation of riboflavin (vitamin B2) was transitioned to engineered Bacillus subtilis production strains.
Violacein, the violet bis-indole pigment of Chromobacterium violaceum, was isolated in crystalline form and shown to possess antibacterial activity.
Paracoccus zeaxanthinifaciens ATCC 21588, isolated from New Caledonia, is a marine bacterium producing (3R,3'R)-zeaxanthin as its predominant carotenoid.

Commercial botulinum neurotoxin type A (Botox/Oculinum) is purified directly from native anaerobic fermentation of wild-type Clostridium botulinum strain Hall A (ATCC 3502), originally isolated in the United States in 1922 (Schantz & Johnson, 1992).

RimabotulinumtoxinB (Myobloc) is a native neurotoxin complex purified from wild-type Clostridium botulinum type B strain Bean fermentation cultures and approved by the FDA in 2000 for cervical dystonia.

Nisin, a 34-residue Type A(I) lantibiotic bacteriocin produced by Lactococcus lactis subsp. lactis, was first identified in 1928 in fermented milk starter cultures in England (Rogers & Whittier, 1928) and commercialized in 1953 as food biopreservative E234.

Native bacterial L-asparaginase purified from Escherichia coli (and Dickeya chrysanthemi) exhibits potent antileukemic activity (Mashburn & Wriston, 1964; Wade et al., 1968) and was commercialized as Elspar/Erwinaze for acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

Streptokinase is a native plasminogen-activating thrombolytic protein produced by beta-hemolytic Streptococcus equisimilis strain H46A (ATCC 12449), discovered by Tillett & Garner (1933) and commercialized for myocardial infarction.

Bacterial hyaluronate lyase (hyaluronidase) produced by Streptomyces hyalurolyticus FERM-P 240, isolated from soil in Japan (Ohya & Kaneko, 1970), is commercialized as a tissue-permeability therapeutic and diagnostic enzyme.
Pediocin PA-1 is a Class IIa anti-listerial bacteriocin produced by Pediococcus acidilactici PAC 1.0 (Gonzalez & Kunka, 1987) and commercialized as a natural food biopreservative (Alta 2341).

Vancomycin is a glycopeptide antibiotic produced by Amycolatopsis orientalis (formerly Streptomyces orientalis), isolated in 1953 from Borneo jungle soil by Eli Lilly (McCormick et al., 1956) and approved in 1958.

Daptomycin is a cyclic lipopeptide antibiotic (factor A21978C1) produced by Streptomyces roseosporus NRRL 11379, isolated from a soil sample collected at Mount Ararat, Turkey (Debono et al., 1988; Eisenstein et al., 2010).

Teicoplanin is a glycopeptide antibiotic complex produced by Actinoplanes teichomyceticus ATCC 31121, isolated from soil collected in Nimodi Village, Indore, India (Parenti et al., 1978) and commercialized in Europe in 1988.

Amphotericin B is a polyene macrolide antifungal produced by Streptomyces nodosus ATCC 14899, isolated in 1955 from soil collected near the Orinoco River in Venezuela (Gold et al., 1956; Trejo & Bennett, 1963).

Nystatin is a polyene macrolide antifungal produced by Streptomyces noursei ATCC 11455, isolated from dairy farm soil in Fauquier County, Virginia, USA (Hazen & Brown, 1950) and commercialized in 1954.

Chlortetracycline (Aureomycin), the first broad-spectrum tetracycline antibiotic, is produced by Streptomyces aureofaciens A-377 (ATCC 10762), isolated in 1945 from soil at Sanborn Field, Columbia, Missouri, USA (Duggar, 1948).
Parent tetracycline is produced via direct native fermentation of Streptomyces viridifaciens ATCC 11989 (and low-chloride Streptomyces aureofaciens fermentation), commercialized in 1954.

Daunorubicin is an anthracycline antitumor antibiotic produced by Streptomyces peucetius ATCC 29050, isolated in 1962 from soil near Castel del Monte, Apulia, Italy (Grein et al., 1963; Di Marco et al., 1964).

Doxorubicin (Adriamycin) is produced by fermentation of Streptomyces peucetius var. caesius ATCC 27952, derived from the Castel del Monte Apulia soil isolate (Arcamone et al., 1969) and approved by the FDA in 1974.

Thiostrepton is a thiopeptide antibiotic produced by Streptomyces azureus ATCC 14921, isolated from soil collected in New Mexico, USA (Pagano et al., 1956) and commercialized in veterinary topical therapeutics.

Monensin is a polyether ionophore anticoccidial and feed-efficiency agent produced by Streptomyces cinnamonensis ATCC 15413 (Haney & Hoehn, 1967; Agtarap et al., 1967), commercialized by Eli Lilly in 1971.

Salinomycin is a polyether ionophore veterinary coccidiostat produced by Streptomyces albus No. 80614 (ATCC 21838), isolated from a soil sample collected in Fuji City, Shizuoka Prefecture, Japan (Miyazaki et al., 1974).
Pristinamycin is a streptogramin antibiotic complex produced by Streptomyces pristinaespiralis ATCC 25486, discovered by Rhone-Poulenc in France and commercialized as Pyostacine in 1962.

Virginiamycin (staphylomycin) is a streptogramin antibiotic complex produced by Streptomyces virginiae ATCC 13161, isolated from Belgian soil by De Somer & Van Dijck (1955) and widely commercialized in animal health.
Tyrothricin (comprising gramicidin and tyrocidine) was the first clinically commercialized bacterial antibiotic, isolated from soil Brevibacillus brevis ATCC 8185 by Rene Dubos (1939).

Colistin (polymyxin E) is a cyclic lipopeptide antibiotic produced by Paenibacillus polymyxa subsp. colistinus, isolated from soil in Fukushima Prefecture, Japan by Koyama et al. (1950) and commercialized in 1959.

isolation_locality: Garden of the Gods, Colorado Springs, Colorado
verbatim_evidence_quote: Ristocetin is a glycopeptide produced by Amycolatopsis lurida NRRL 2430, isolated from soil in Colorado Springs, Colorado, USA (Philip et al., 1957) and commercialized clinically and as the gold-standard von Willebrand factor platelet aggregation diagnostic.
Josamycin is a 16-membered macrolide antibiotic produced by Streptomyces narbonensis var. josamyceticus ATCC 17835, isolated from soil in Japan (Osono et al., 1967) and commercialized in 1970.

Spiramycin is a 16-membered macrolide antibiotic produced by Streptomyces ambofaciens ATCC 23877, isolated from soil in France by Pinnert-Sindico et al. (1954) and commercialized as Rovamycine in 1955.

Midecamycin (SF-837) is a 16-membered macrolide antibiotic produced by Streptomyces mycarofaciens ATCC 21454, isolated from soil in Japan by Meiji Seika (Tsuruoka et al., 1971) and commercialized in 1974.

Aclacinomycin A (aclarubicin) is an anthracycline antitumor antibiotic produced by Streptomyces galilaeus MA144-M1 (ATCC 31133), isolated from soil in Tokyo, Japan (Oki et al., 1975) and commercialized in 1981.
Mithramycin (plicamycin) is an aureolic acid polyketide antineoplastic agent produced by Streptomyces argillaceus ATCC 12956 (Rao et al., 1962) and approved by the FDA in 1970.

Streptozotocin (Zanosar) is a naturally occurring glucosamine-nitrosourea produced by Streptomyces achromogenes var. streptozoticus NRRL 2697, isolated from soil in Blue Rapids, Kansas, USA (Vavra et al., 1960; Herr et al., 1967).

Acarbose (Glucobay/Precose) is a pseudotetrasaccharide alpha-glucosidase inhibitor produced by native fermentation of Actinoplanes sp. SE50/110, isolated from soil collected in Ruiru, Kenya (Schmidt et al., 1977).
Industrial Vitamin B12 (cyanocobalamin) is produced exclusively via bacterial fermentation using Propionibacterium freudenreichii subsp. shermanii and Pseudomonas denitrificans (Rickes et al., 1948).
Tylosin is a 16-membered macrolide veterinary antibiotic and feed additive produced natively by Streptomyces fradiae ATCC 19609, isolated from soil collected in Thailand (McGuire et al., 1961).
Lasalocid A (Bovatec/Avatec) is a polyether ionophore coccidiostat produced natively by Streptomyces lasaliensis ATCC 31180, isolated from soil in Hyde Park, Massachusetts, USA (Berger et al., 1951).
A thermostable bacterial alpha-amylase (Termamyl) was developed from a selected strain of Bacillus licheniformis by Novo Industri.
Thermostable cobalt-containing nitrile hydratase from Pseudonocardia thermophila JCM 3095 is utilized industrially for acrylamide manufacture.

envo_material_id: human war wound / gas gangrene exudate
verbatim_evidence_quote: Clostridium histolyticum (isolated from human war wounds in France) produces commercial collagenases ColG and ColH used in wound debridement and Dupuytren's contracture.

isolation_locality: Mushroom Spring, Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming
envo_material_id: thermal hot spring water / microbial mat
verbatim_evidence_quote: Thermus aquaticus YT-1 was isolated from Mushroom Spring in Yellowstone National Park and yields thermostable Taq DNA polymerase for PCR.
Esterase EstB from Burkholderia gladioli was developed by Roche Diagnostics for industrial deacetylation of cephalosporin intermediates.

canonical_name: High-molecular weight cobalt-containing nitrile hydratase subunit alpha
verbatim_evidence_quote: Rhodococcus rhodochrous J1, isolated from soil in Japan, produces high-molecular-weight cobalt nitrile hydratase used commercially to manufacture acrylamide and nicotinamide.
Iron-containing nitrile hydratase from Rhodococcus sp. N-774 / Brevibacterium R312 launched the first industrial enzymatic process for acrylamide production in Japan.
Phospholipase D from Streptomyces antibioticus is used industrially for enzymatic transphosphatidylation to manufacture phosphatidylserine.
Escherichia coli periplasmic phosphoanhydride phosphohydrolase (AppA) is widely commercialized as a feed-grade 6-phytase in animal nutrition.
Subtilisin BPN' (Nagarse) is an alkaline serine protease isolated from Bacillus amyloliquefaciens in Japan for industrial detergent and protein hydrolysis.
Subtilisin Carlsberg (commercialized as Alcalase) was discovered at the Carlsberg Laboratory in Copenhagen from Bacillus licheniformis.
Savinase is a high-alkaline detergent protease isolated from alkaliphilic Bacillus lentus (Lederbergia lenta) by Novo Industri.

Calcium-independent microbial transglutaminase (mTGase) produced by Streptomyces mobaraensis S-8112 (Ando et al., 1989, Agric. Biol. Chem. 53:2613-2617) is commercialized worldwide for food protein cross-linking.

D-Xylose isomerase (glucose isomerase) produced commercially by Streptomyces rubiginosus ATCC 21175 and Actinoplanes missouriensis (Takasaki, 1966; Marshall & Kooi, 1957) drives industrial high-fructose corn syrup manufacturing.

Pullulanase, a starch-debranching enzyme discovered in Klebsiella aerogenes (Aerobacter aerogenes; Bender & Wallenfels, 1961) and commercialized alongside Bacillus acidopullulyticus (Jensen & Norman, 1984), is used in industrial starch saccharification.

Cyclodextrin glycosyltransferase (CGTase), produced by Paenibacillus macerans (Bacillus macerans; Schardinger, 1903; Tilden & Hudson, 1939) and Bacillus circulans, is used for industrial cyclodextrin manufacturing.

Thermolysin is a thermostable neutral metalloprotease produced by Bacillus thermoproteolyticus (Geobacillus stearothermophilus), isolated from Rokko, Japan (Endo, 1962) and commercialized for enzymatic Z-aspartame precursor synthesis.

Penicillin G acylase produced by Escherichia coli ATCC 11105 and Bacillus megaterium (Kaufmann & Bauer, 1960; Rolinson et al., 1960) is the primary industrial biocatalyst for 6-aminopenicillanic acid (6-APA) manufacture.

Bacterial D-hydantoinase coupled with D-carbamoylase from Agrobacterium radiobacter NRRL B-11291 (Olivieri et al., 1981) is used industrially to synthesize D-phenylglycine and D-p-hydroxyphenylglycine for semi-synthetic beta-lactam antibiotics.
Bacterial aspartase (L-aspartate ammonia-lyase) from Escherichia coli (Chibata et al., 1974) pioneered continuous immobilized biocatalysis in Japan for industrial L-aspartic acid production.
L-Aspartate beta-decarboxylase from Pseudomonas dacunhae IAM 1152 (Chibata et al., 1965) is used industrially for enzymatic decarboxylation of L-aspartate to L-alanine.
Bacterial L-aminoacylase from Alcaligenes and Pseudomonas strains is employed in industrial enzymatic membrane reactors for chiral optical resolution of N-acyl-DL-amino acids.
Bacterial beta-galactosidase produced by Bacillus circulans ATCC 31382 (Mozaffar et al., 1984) is commercialized globally for lactose hydrolysis and prebiotic galacto-oligosaccharide (GOS) synthesis.
Alkaline endo-1,4-beta-mannanase isolated from alkaliphilic Bacillus sp. AM-001 in Japan (Akino et al., 1987) is commercialized in laundry detergents and animal feed formulations.
Alkaline bacterial pectate lyase from Bacillus sp. (Nasser et al., 1990) is commercialized for enzymatic textile cotton bioscouring and fruit juice clarification.
Alkaline cellulase discovered in alkaliphilic Bacillus sp. N-4 by Horikoshi et al. (1984) was commercialized by Kao Corporation (Attack detergent) in 1987 for fabric care and soil release.
Alkaline bacterial lipases from Burkholderia cepacia and Pseudomonas alcaligenes (Gerritse et al., 1998) are commercialized as lipid-stain-degrading enzymes in heavy-duty laundry detergents.

Keratinase KerA produced by Bacillus licheniformis PWD-1 (ATCC 53757), isolated from a poultry waste digester in North Carolina (Williams et al., 1990), is commercialized for feather-meal feed processing.

Bacterial urate oxidase (uricase) produced by Arthrobacter globiformis and Bacillus fastidiosus (Mahler, 1963) is commercialized as a clinical diagnostic reagent and therapeutic uric acid-lowering enzyme.

Bacterial cholesterol oxidase produced by Rhodococcus erythropolis (Nocardia erythropolis; Richmond, 1973) and Streptomyces sp. is the standard enzymatic reagent for clinical serum cholesterol assays.
